Priya to provide list of compliance questions for SOC2/HIPAA review, Cc Redwood security

summary: Renewal heartbeat for upcoming contract renewal; customer interested in capacity upgrade to support additional regions (EU + APAC), discussing Dedicated reserved capacity vs multi-region hosted routing, and a potential 12-month extension with a higher committed spend for discounted unit pricing. Security team raised SOC2 and KMS questions; SE to run benchmark tests for 16k-context model to validate p99 latency and cost. Next steps: pricing options, benchmarks, and compliance questionnaire.
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-06
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Owen Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Liu (Redwood CSM), Lara Kim (Valen Head of MLOps), Derek Shaw (Valen CTO), Priya Nair (Valen Security Lead), Marco Ruiz (Valen SRE)
Recording: enabled
Location: Zoom
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I see we have the usual crew from Valen, thanks for making time. quick agenda: renewal check-in, capacity needs, multi-region ask, and any security questions.
[00:18] Derek Shaw: Yeah thanks Maya, quick FYI we're on a tight timeline, renewal hits end of month and we'd like to lock something early to avoid any -- you know -- service churn during our Q2 ramp.
[00:29] Maya Chen: Totally understood; goal is to make that easy. Owen, do you want to kick off with the capacity options?
[00:35] Owen Patel: Sure; hi everyone. So from the technical side Valen's traffic has grown about 2.6x since last renewal, and you're seeing heavier long-context runs -- the 16k token models for conversational retrieval are becoming a big part of cost. The options are basically: stay hosted and use smart routing to route some traffic to lower-cost regions, buy Dedicated reserved capacity to guarantee throughput, or go Private for on-prem/VPC which I know you asked about last quarter.
[01:05] Lara Kim: Yeah we ran a pilot of the 16k model last month, p50 is okay but p99 spikes and it impacts UX. We're leaning Dedicated since predictable latency's important, but we also need EU region support and want to test APAC in Q3.
[01:20] Owen Patel: That makes sense. For Dedicated we can provision GPU pools across us-west and eu-west, and add a third pool in ap-southeast during Q3. We have two deployment strategies: single reserved pool with cross-region failover, or dedicated reserved per region. Per-region reserved gives better p99 but higher commit. There's also an option where you keep hosted for non-critical low-latency paths and overflow to Dedicated for high-priority long-context sessions.
[01:52] Derek Shaw: Cost math is the big blocker. If we commit more, what's the unit price delta, and can we get a discount tied to a 12-month extension?
[02:02] Maya Chen: Yes, we typically offer tiered discounts for committed spend. I'll send three pricing options: (1) minimal renewal with small commitment and host-only routing, (2) Dedicated 2-region commit (US + EU) with burst to hosted and (3) Full 3-region Dedicated commit (US, EU, APAC) with deeper discounts. Each option will include projected token/unit costs and an estimate of expected p99 improvements based on past runs.
[02:26] Priya Nair: On security, quick things -- SOC2 type II evidence, KMS integration details (customer-managed keys), audit logs retention, and egress controls for EU data. We need explicit confirmation about logs retention for Private vs Dedicated vs Hosted.
[02:41] Owen Patel: For Dedicated we provide audit logs and can integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. Hosted keeps logs for X days by default but we can increase retention as a part of an add-on; for Private you control logs and retention. I'll attach the security spec and a short matrix showing what is available per deployment type.
[03:01] Marco Ruiz: Also wanted to flag networking -- for Dedicated in EU we need the VPC peering setup and support for our firewall rules; how long does that usually take?
[03:11] Maya Chen: VPC peering usually is 2-3 weeks once networking configs are finalized. If you want APAC soon we should start provisioning conversations this week to hit Q3.
[03:21] Lara Kim: That timeline sounds tight but doable. On benchmarking, can you reproduce our 16k token load profile? We have a lot of conversational history reuse, so KV cache behavior matters a lot.
[03:34] Owen Patel: Yes we'll replicate your token distributions; if you share a sample traffic profile and token distribution CSV Marco mentioned, we'll run the same batch and streaming profiles. I'll include both p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost breakdowns.
[03:48] Derek Shaw: If benchmarks show p99 under our SLO on Dedicated, we can likely go with a 12-month higher commit. What's the usual SLA uplift for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:57] Sara Liu: For Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime and latency targets with an SLO-based credit mechanism; hosted has standard availability guarantees but not the same per-tenant p99 commitments. We'll include SLA language in the pricing packet.
[04:10] Priya Nair: A couple more security clarifications -- can Redwood support our internal HSM for key wrap, or do you require keys be in Redwood-managed KMS? Also need details on data residency guarantees for EU-only workloads.
[04:23] Owen Patel: We support customer-managed keys via standard KMS integrations; for HSM key wrapping we'd need to validate the exact provider but it's possible via our KMS bridge. For EU-only workloads we can pin Dedicated pools to eu-west and ensure routing policy keeps data local; we'll include the data flow diagram in the docs.
[04:40] Derek Shaw: Great. On procurement, if we expand commit, how long is the contract extension process? We have procurement calendars to hit.
[04:49] Maya Chen: For renewals and extensions we usually have a 1-2 week legal review for standard T&Cs; when redlines come in it can extend; for enterprise deals we pre-stage SOWs which can speed it up. If you need faster turnaround we can loop in our contracts teammate and prioritize.
[05:05] Lara Kim: Let's talk operationally: during the last month we saw a couple of token mismatches where the KV cache evictions caused duplicate upstream fetches, raising cost. Any config knobs?
[05:18] Owen Patel: We have cache tuning -- prefix caching TTLs, soft eviction thresholds, and adaptive batching. We'll propose quantization/packing changes for the models too; that often reduces GPU memory pressure and improves throughput. But we should test on your payloads.
[05:33] Marco Ruiz: For the APAC region, are there any expected capacity lead times for certain GPUs? We've previously seen backlog for A100-like instances.
[05:42] Owen Patel: Good point. APAC capacity can be constrained; for Dedicated we can reserve capacity ahead of time but it will up the commit. If APAC is critical Q3, I'd recommend provisioning now. We'll include projected provisioning lead times in the doc.
[05:56] Priya Nair: On compliance, we might need HIPAA addendum if we route PHI. Does Redwood have BAAs?
[06:03] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood can provide a BAA for HIPAA-covered use cases per our enterprise package. We'll route that to legal and include the BAA draft.
[06:12] Derek Shaw: Okay sounds good. Any blockers on Redwood's side to produce the benchmark and pricing?
[06:18] Maya Chen: No blockers; Owen will run the bench as soon as you share the profile and we'll produce numbers in 48-72 hours. We'll aim to get the pricing sheet and SLA language to you by Tuesday (2026-03-10).
[06:29] Owen Patel: Quick note -- the 16k model results vary a lot with effective batch size; please include expected concurrency and steady-state tokens per second in the profile.
[06:38] Lara Kim: We'll send concurrency targets -- currently 120 concurrent chat sessions at peak with mean tokens per turn ~ 320 and average turns per session of 8.
[06:47] Maya Chen: Perfect. Anything else from Valen?
[06:50] Priya Nair: One ask -- can you include an explicit audit log retention table for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Our audit team needs that to sign off.
[06:58] Owen Patel: Yes will include a matrix for retention, granularity, and export formats.
[07:05] Marco Ruiz: And please include network diagram for VPC peering step-by-step so our infra team can plan firewall rules.
[07:12] Maya Chen: Will do. Last thing -- recap and next steps.
[07:16] Maya Chen: Recap: Maya will send three pricing options and SLA language by 2026-03-10; Owen will run benchmarks after Valen shares traffic CSV and concurrency targets, deliverable 2026-03-09; Priya will send compliance questions by 2026-03-12; Marco to send token distribution CSV by 2026-03-08.
[07:33] Derek Shaw: Thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround. If the numbers align we'll sign a 12-month extension with a 2-region Dedicated commit and add APAC provision in Q3.
[07:45] Maya Chen: Great, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM. Thanks everyone.
[07:50] End of recording.
